name: Arjun Mehta
self_assessment: I shipped the new dashboard redesign this year, which improved page-load time by 42% and raised our accessibility score from 71 to 96. I picked up on-call duties for the web platform in Q1 and closed 34 bugs during the March quality sprint. I feel my work is solid but I don't think my manager sees much of it since we moved to different office floors in April.

manager_feedback.text: Arjun consistently underperforms compared to the rest of the team. He doesn't seem engaged and I rarely see him contributing in meetings. I have concerns about his commitment.

peer_feedback.text: Arjun single-handedly drove the dashboard redesign — 42% faster page loads and the accessibility score went from 71 to 96, which unblocked the enterprise deal with Northstar. He pairs with me weekly and unblocked my chart-rendering bug in an afternoon after I'd been stuck for two days.

During the March quality sprint Arjun closed 34 bugs — the highest on the team — including the long-standing Safari checkout rendering bug that support had 60+ tickets on. He writes the most testable frontend code on the team.

Arjun is quiet in large meetings but incredibly effective async — his RFC comments on the dashboard redesign caught two UX issues before we built them. He prototyped three design options in a week when we were stuck.

goals.goal: Ship dashboard redesign by end of Q2
goals.evidence: Shipped 2026-05-20. Page-load time improved 42% (3.1s → 1.8s); Lighthouse accessibility score 71 → 96.

goals.goal: Reduce open frontend bug backlog by 25%
goals.evidence: Backlog reduced 31% (178 → 123 bugs), driven largely by Arjun's 34 closed bugs in the March quality sprint.

project_outcomes.outcome: Shipped on time; 42% page-load improvement; accessibility 71 → 96; cited by sales as a factor in closing the Northstar enterprise deal.
Arjun closed 34 bugs (team high), including the Safari checkout bug behind 60+ support tickets.
